definitions.explanation: A general term for dishes that are primarily liquid, such as miso soup, clear soup, or various broths served as part of a Japanese meal.

examples.japanese: {和食|わしょく}の{献立|こんだて}には{汁物|しるもの}が{欠|か}かせない。
examples.english: A soup dish is essential in a Japanese meal.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}の{汁物|しるもの}は{豚汁|とんじる}です。
examples.english: Today's soup dish is pork miso soup.

examples.japanese: {一汁三菜|いちじゅうさんさい}の「{汁|しる}」は{汁物|しるもの}のことだ。
examples.english: The 'soup' in 'one soup, three dishes' refers to a soup dish.

notes:
USAGE: {汁物|しるもの} is a category term used in {和食|わしょく} (Japanese cuisine) to describe any soup or liquid-based dish. It is one of the core components of a traditional Japanese meal.

COMMON TYPES:
・{味噌汁|みそしる} (miso soup)
・{吸|す}い{物|もの}/{お吸|す}い{物|もの} (clear soup)
・{豚汁|とんじる}/{とん{汁|じる}} (pork miso soup)
・{けんちん{汁|じる}} (vegetable soup with tofu)
・{粕汁|かすじる} (sake lees soup)

CULTURAL CONTEXT:
{一汁三菜|いちじゅうさんさい} (one soup, three side dishes) is the traditional format for a Japanese meal:
・{飯|はん} (rice) - main starch
・{汁物|しるもの} (soup) - liquid dish
・{菜|さい} (three side dishes) - vegetables, protein, etc.

This balanced format is still considered the ideal for healthy Japanese home cooking.
